summary: Yoshiyasu Yonezawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998-2006) and as a specially appointed full-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe earned a doctorate in science at Tohoku University (~1970-1975). He worked at Tohoku University as an assistant (1975-2012) and senior research fellow (2018), held posts at UC Berkeley and JAIST, and founded the ACCMS.

Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1935-1939). He served as a professor at Rissho University (~1961-1987) and as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1977-1988).

Youlan Feng worked in philosophy and Sinology. He studied at Peking University and Columbia University, among other institutions, and held posts at Tsinghua University (~1928-1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946-1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1946-1947).

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, later serving at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.
Youwei Kang worked in philosophy, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He founded the Wanmu Caotang in 1890, taught there from ~1891 to 1898, and taught Qichao Liang.

Yozo Taniyama is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1991-1996). He held posts at Tohoku University (~2011), St. Thomas University, Japan (~2008-2010), International Buddhist University, and Sophia University.

Yu Yan Pang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. Pang earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's study at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü. Tsui also studied under doctoral supervisor Natasha Heller (attested 2018) and traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-guang Liu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Liu studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 under Samten, Tashi Tsering, Gongbaojie, and Gyalog, and earned a PhD from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).

Yu-kwan Ng studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD at McMaster University. Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Ng held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~2001-2016).

Yu-min Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Lee studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington, taught Pei-jung Wu, and served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Ren earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the doctoral supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo (1920-1982) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Gongga Rinpoche and Gangkar Rinpoche, and held positions at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism and the Jinling Scriptural Press.

Yuanying Shi was a Buddhist studies figure who served as abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples. He was president of the Buddhist Association of China (1929; 1953) and founded the Sengmin School and Yuanming Lengyan School.

Yudru Tsomu is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She completed a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, with advisors Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn, and taught Hoong Teik Toh.

Yuen Ren Chao was a linguist and Sinologist who studied at Cornell and Harvard universities. He held academic posts at Cornell (~1919-1920), Harvard (~1921-1924), Tsinghua University (~1925-1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947-1963).
Yuexia was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served as a teacher there.
Yuhiko Katsuzaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from ~1964 to 1974. He later served as the president of Taisho University from ~2010 to 2014.
Yui Chi Lau was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Yingguang Qu. Lau founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society and taught Shek-wing Tam.
